request.spec:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Transferring a person to a sheet that already has someone with the same name or alias (ignoring case) now merges them into that person instead of refusing. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What a merging transfer does** (in `PersonTransferService.java`):
- The arriving claims go to the matching person, listed after that person's own claims. Numbered claims get the next numbers on the other sheet, in the order they were opened. Figures a statement had bound are lost.
- The arriving name and aliases become aliases of the matching person. Their grades, terms and contact are dropped, as in a normal merge.
- The other sheet's audit gets `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … name=<name> from=<sheet>`, then `PERSON_MERGED … from=<name> into=<name>`, then the rollup lines. The source sheet's audit records are unchanged.

**Still refused**, because none of these has a clear merge target. I chose these rules myself (the request doesn't cover them), so check they're what you want:
- the arriving names match more than one person on the other sheet;
- the matching person is retired (an ordinary merge refuses this too);
- a name is used on another sheet in the other sheet's tree;
- the arriving contact belongs to someone other than the matching person.

**Schema change:** the test expects a person to end up with aliases "Addie" and "addie", which the old rule (no two aliases on a person differing only by case) didn't allow. A new migration, `V73__person_alias_exact.sql`, now only blocks exact duplicates. Adding an alias through the screen still refuses case variants, because the app checks for those before saving.

The front end needed no changes.
